title: How to Read a Jain Manuscript

overview.historical_context: teachings of the Jinas were initially transmitted orally. They were committed to writing around the 5th century CE, though most surviving manuscripts date from the 11th century CE onward.

core_distinction.text: Relates to the conceptual contents of the work.
core_distinction.manuscript: Relates to the physical object itself (a late manuscript can contain a very ancient text).

scripts.style_variant: Jain Nāgarī (characterized by distinctive letter shapes unique to Jain scribes)

folio_structure.definition: Loose sheets with two sides: Recto (front / A side) and Verso (back / B side).
folio_structure.numbering_placement: Generally located on the verso side.

systems.characteristic_medium: Palm-leaf manuscripts (and exceptionally old 15th-century paper manuscripts).
systems.logic: Distinct letters represent numbers 1-10, multiples of 10 (20, 30, etc.), and hundreds up to 400. Multi-digit numbers are stacked vertically.
Uses numeric digits, though some figures match the distinct 'Jain Nāgarī' styling.

beginning.auspicious_sign: Conventionally transcribed as 'Bhale' (exact historic meaning remains debated).
beginning.invocation_phrase: Pays homage to a specific Jina or Hindu protective deities like Gaṇeśa or Sarasvatī. Formulas include 'Oṃ namo Vardhamānāya' or 'Oṃ namo Gaṇeśāya'.

margins.dimensions: Average of 5 centimeters of empty space above, below, and to the sides.
margins.framing: Often marked out by two double vertical lines.

marginalia_commentary_styles.tri_patha: Three readings: The main text runs through the center, while large top and bottom margins host running commentaries in minute script.
marginalia_commentary_styles.panca_patha: Five readings: Main text in the center, with commentaries filling all four margins. Readers follow a specific layout sequence: Top -> Right -> Left -> Bottom.

text_body.word_spacing: Continuous script (Scriptio continua) without spaces between words. Later readers sometimes added small vertical strokes above letters as word-dividers.
text_body.punctuation: Uses single or double vertical lines known as 'Daṇḍa' (stick) in black or red ink. Single daṇḍa indicates the end of a verse segment (pāda); double daṇḍa marks the end of a complete verse.
text_body.verse_numbering: Stanza numbers are indicated at the end of the verse rather than the beginning.
text_body.chapter_ends: Section titles/numbers are marked at the conclusion of a chapter, often highlighted using red or orange powder.

central_space.visuals: A blank square, rectangle, or lozenge cutout in the direct center of the page. Can be empty, filled with red discs, or contain stylized geometric/artistic lettering.
central_space.historical_origin: A structural carryover mimicking the central hole used in older palm-leaf manuscripts to thread a binding cord.

paintings_and_illustrations.dimensions: Standardized size of roughly 10 x 8 centimeters, bound by rectangular lines.
paintings_and_illustrations.placement: Typically on the left or right of the text block.
paintings_and_illustrations.captions: Written in small script along the side margins, likely added by either the scribe or painter as cross-reference guidance.

provenance_and_colophons.colophon_definition: A publication block located at the absolute end of the manuscript providing creation and lineage details.

metadata_tracked.title: Rarely at the beginning; usually follows the term 'iti' (meaning 'thus') at the end of a work or specific section.
metadata_tracked.author: Stated at the end of text blocks. Monks are frequently accompanied by highly stylized praise formulas called 'Praśastis'.
metadata_tracked.scribe: Indicated via the formula 'likhitam by X' (copied by X). Scribes were either professional copyists or Jain monks noting their lineage.
metadata_tracked.sponsors: Mentions names and abbreviated social statuses of the patrons who commissioned the work.
metadata_tracked.owners_and_readers: Reflects lineage of ownership, often written in multiple handwritings. Former names were occasionally erased using white or yellow pigments.
metadata_tracked.library_references: Local classification markings typically written as 'manuscript number X, box number X', denoting the historical temple library storage chests.
